description: The Matrix is a team of passionate IT students and technology enthusiasts participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are interested in AI/ML, data science, software development, space technology, and solving real-world problems through innovative solutions.
summary:
Space Relics 3D is an interactive 3D Solar System exploration platform that brings humanity's space exploration history into one immersive environment.

Users can explore planets and discover the spacecraft, rovers, landers, orbiters, satellites, telescopes, probes, helicopters, and space stations associated with them.

The platform features a structured catalogue of 211 space missions, 460 moons, 19 space stations, and 41 launch vehicles. Users can interact with individual objects to access their mission records, photographs, scientific information, and exploration history.

An integrated AI Mission Guide helps users understand space missions, compare spacecraft, explore planetary destinations, and learn about humanity's achievements in space exploration.

By combining interactive 3D visualization, structured scientific information, and conversational learning, Space Relics 3D makes space exploration more accessible, engaging, and understandable.
details:
Overview

Space Relics 3D is an interactive three-dimensional Solar System explorer designed to make space exploration history accessible through immersive visualization and structured scientific information.

Instead of presenting planets and space missions as disconnected facts, the platform connects exploration hardware with its respective celestial destinations, allowing users to discover humanity's space exploration achievements in a unified environment.

Key Features

1. Interactive 3D Solar System

A realistic 3D environment featuring planets, dwarf planets, moons, planetary atmospheres, rings, orbital paths, and a starfield. Users can navigate the environment through interactive camera controls.

2. Space Mission Catalogue

Explore a structured collection of 211 space missions, including rovers, landers, orbiters, probes, satellites, telescopes, and other exploration hardware.

3. Scientific Information and Position Visualization

The platform incorporates published landing-site coordinates and orbital elements to visualize the locations of exploration missions and space stations. Position information is presented with precision indicators to distinguish measured, reported, approximate, and unpublished positions.

4. AI Mission Guide

An integrated conversational guide helps users explore mission records, spacecraft achievements, mission status, planetary destinations, and comparisons between missions.

The guide prioritizes the platform's structured dataset and supplements it with external educational information when necessary.

5. Photographic Mission Records

Users can open individual spacecraft records and explore associated photographs, mission details, and historical information.

Technology

  • React and Vite
  • Three.js
  • React Three Fiber
  • Drei
  • JavaScript
  • Structured JSON datasets
  • Browser-based AI Mission Guide

Impact

Space Relics 3D aims to make planetary exploration and space mission history easier to understand through interactive learning.

It provides students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and curious users with a unified environment to explore spacecraft, understand their destinations, and discover the scientific achievements behind humanity's exploration of the Solar System.

Future Development

Potential future improvements include expanding mission datasets, incorporating additional space agency resources, improving educational features, and adding more detailed mission visualization capabilities.
